title: Galatea Systems - Private Onramp & Regions Intake
summary: Intro discovery focused on private/VPC onramp options for Redwood Private, region restrictions (EU/APAC), network topology choices (transit gateway vs peering), and security requirements (KMS, SOC 2, SSO). Customer is leaning toward Private deployment but wants to evaluate hosted fallback and Dedicated reserved capacity pricing. Agreed to a short pilot for a single EU region with benchmarking and a deeper network session with their networking team.
topics: Private endpoints and private link mechanics
action_items: Alex Moreno: Send Redwood Private network prerequisites doc and sample VPC diagram (due 2027-12-02)
Priya Shah: Prepare estimated pricing for Dedicated reserved pool for 2x GPUs in eu-west-1 and hosted fallback options (due 2027-12-06)
Marcus Lee: Share internal network topology and current Transit GW/Direct Connect details (due 2027-12-01)
Lina Park: List compliance needs (SOC2 controls, any PCI/PHI constraints) and KMS preferences (due 2027-12-04)
next_steps: Schedule a deep-dive network workshop with Galatea networking team next week
Provision a pilot in eu-west-1 for performance/egress benchmarking
Redwood to share security package, SOC2 report, and HSM/KMS integration notes
Follow up with pricing and pilot SOW draft
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-29
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Galatea Head of Infra), Lina (Galatea Security), Tom (CTO)

Summary auto: quick intake on private onramp, region gating, and security.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick round robin — do I have the right folks for network and security?
[00:08] Marcus: Yep Marcus here, I run infra. Lina is security, Tom is running point on architecture but he might jump in.
[00:14] Alex: Awesome. Priya will go deep on the network questions after I run through our high level options.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick note — we'll cover Private deployment patterns, peering vs transit, private endpoints, and region constraints. Also happy to talk about Dedicated reserved capacity if you want predictable throughput.
[00:31] Tom (Galatea CTO): We're primarily looking at keeping data in EU and UK, maybe APAC later. Security and auditability are big; we need KMS and strong logging. Latency to our services in eu-west-1 matters for some user-facing features.
[00:45] Alex: Great, that's helpful. Marcus, can you describe your current network? Are you on a Transit Gateway or pure peering? Any Direct Connect?
[00:52] Marcus: We have a Transit GW in AWS, a few DX circuits in eu-west-1 and eu-central, and peering into some partners. We also have an on-prem MPLS edge in a couple regions. Hoping to avoid hairpinning.
[01:05] Priya: Ok, so transit gateway is common. Two main Redwood Private patterns: 1) VPC peering to our private VPCs with private endpoints, or 2) Customer-managed transit gateway attachments where we peer via TGW attachment or use a partner interconnect. Each has tradeoffs on scale and route propagation.
[01:25] Lina: For us, the key is we cannot have data egress to another country without controls. We need to ensure the model execution and KV cache never leave the EU region for EU traffic. Do you support region pinning?
[01:36] Priya: Yes, we support model pinning to regions. For Private deploy, you can pin a model and have a single-region footprint. We do offer cross-region fallback but that would be opt-in and we'd surface where execution happened for auditing.
[01:47] Tom: How does private endpoints work — is it like AWS PrivateLink or something vendor-specific?
[01:52] Priya: We expose Private Endpoints in your VPC — it's essentially PrivateLink/Interface endpoints. Traffic stays on the AWS network, no public internet hops. For other clouds it's analogous (e.g., Azure Private Link, GCP Private Service Connect).
[02:05] Marcus: What's your recommended pattern if we have lots of VPCs? We have 12 account VPCs that need access to the inference endpoints.
[02:12] Priya: For 12 VPCs at scale, Transit GW with TGW attachments is usually cleaner — a shared services VPC and route tables. Peering can work but becomes n^2 as you grow. Our engineers have done both.
[02:24] Alex: Also note Dedicated reserved pools can live in a private VPC controlled by you so compute stays inside your network fabric. Hosted has simpler onboarding but you send requests over our hosted endpoints, though we offer private link options even for hosted in some regions.
[02:38] Lina: About keys — KMS/HSM. We must manage keys for any cached data and logs. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[02:45] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. For HSM-backed keys or Cloud HSM we can integrate; there is an extra validation step and we ship key usage logs. We'll surface what we're encrypting and where.
[02:58] Tom: For compliance, do you publish SOC2 and pen test reports?
[03:02] Alex: Yes, SOC2 Type II available under NDA. We also have penetration test summaries and can share compliance artifacts as part of the security package.
[03:10] Marcus: Egress costs — important for us. If requests go cross-region or back to hosted, we'd be paying egress on our side and your side. Any suggestions for minimizing that?
[03:20] Priya: Keep compute and callers in same region, use regional private endpoints, and enable prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated tokens. For cross-region fallbacks, we can compress and batch where possible but there will be network costs. In Dedicated, you can configure local-only routes and disable cross-region fallback.
[03:36] Marcus: Bandwidth wise — we plan to do synchronous user-facing generation not massive embedding streams, estimate peaks at ~200 Mbps to the endpoint. Is that reasonable?
[03:45] Priya: That's fine, we typically handle that for a Dedicated pool. We'll want to validate in the pilot. Also ask if you have bursty patterns — autoscaling and burst capacity options exist but with reserved pools you get predictable throughput.
[03:58] Tom: What's the timeline for getting a Private deployment up for a pilot? Weeks? Months?
[04:03] Alex: For a one-region Private pilot with a single VPC endpoint and a small dedicated pool, we can often stand it up in 2-3 weeks once we have network details and an A-team contact. Full production readiness with compliance gating might take longer.
[04:15] Lina: We need to know who in Redwood will own the network handshake and the runbook. Also we need the network prerequisites doc.
[04:22] Alex: Priya will own the technical onboarding and provide the runbook. We'll share network prerequisites and a sample VPC diagram after the call.
[04:29] Marcus: A couple of small gotchas we saw with other vendors — route table limits when using peering, and source/destination checks needing to be disabled on NAT instances. Also we want end-to-end encryption in transit and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[04:42] Priya: Good notes — we surface all of that. We can also configure syslog/audit forwarding or push logs to a dedicated S3 bucket in your account with restricted access.
[04:53] Tom: On the model side, do you host third-party models and also support quantized weights to reduce memory? We may want a smaller footprint for cost reasons.
[05:00] Alex: We host curated open models and can run quantized variants in Dedicated/private. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on quant profiles and batching to reduce unit costs. We'll include suggested configs for your expected prompt lengths.
[05:14] Marcus: If we pick private + dedicated, can we still call out to a hosted fallback during outages?
[05:20] Priya: Yes, that is an option. You can configure fallbacks by policy — e.g., local region first, then dedicated pool in another region, then hosted as last resort. Each step is logged for traceability.
[05:33] Lina: Any concerns about multi-tenant code paths accessing our KV cache?
[05:36] Priya: KV cache is isolated per customer in Private deployments. We'll document the isolation guarantees.
[05:42] Alex: Quick recap — notes: we will share security pack + SOC2, Priya to send network runbook, Marcus to send network topology, Lina will send compliance checklist, Redwood to draft pilot SOW and pricing for a small reserved Dedicated pool in eu-west-1.
[05:56] Tom: That works. One last question — do you support Okta SSO for the console and RBAC for operators?
[06:01] Alex: Yes Okta SAML SSO supported and role-based access controls. We'll share docs.
[06:09] Marcus: Great. Then let's schedule the network deep-dive next Wednesday.
[06:13] Pria (sic - Priya): I'll propose times after the call.
[06:16] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and time proposals.

End of call

Notes on quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (Pria -> Priya, some acronyms), natural crosstalk, timestamps approximate.
